environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; raw socket client and strict upstream peer

findings.description: startup() pops a pooled fd and treats a single recv(fd,&x,1,MSG_PEEK|MSG_DONTWAIT) returning >=0 as proof the socket is idle, then reuses it for the new request. An upstream that writes its response slowly straddles that check: the peek sees the first byte of a still-live response, the proxy still sends the new request on the same socket, and the parser reads the old response as the answer. Result is either a 502 mid-stream or a full response belonging to another client, with the peer log proving both requests were really served. Precondition: pooled upstream reuse and a slow upstream.
findings.title: Pool liveness is one MSG_PEEK byte, so an upstream byte arriving in the peek-to-send window makes the next client receive the previous client's response

findings.description: respond() increments the connection request counter and compares it against cfg.maxreq; the pool index comes from a global round-robin with no Host component, so requests for different host_root values land on the same pooled fd and share that counter. A burst on one vhost therefore ends the keep-alive of a connection another vhost believes is its own. Precondition: pooled reuse with more than one vhost.
findings.title: max_requests is enforced on a per-connection counter but the pool ignores Host, so a bound reached on one vhost retires a socket another vhost is using

findings.description: Same window, other outcome: when only part of a header arrives, the peek succeeds but the new request's response parse starts mid-header, and responseparse fails the client with 502 rather than reuse. Precondition: pooled reuse and an upstream that dribbles bytes.
findings.title: A stray upstream byte in the peek window turns the next request into a 502 instead of a substituted body

limitations: All RCE is on the upstream host
The substitution is racy; hit rate was about 10 in 30 across two clients
Needs a pooled build and two upstreams for the cross-vhost case
